title: Terminal hands-on
question: According to the script's demonstration in Phase 04, what happens when you run sha256sum on a string of text, but change just one letter to a capital? (e.g., "sudo access" vs "sudo Access")
options: The hash flips completely into an unrecognizably different string of characters.
Only the first few characters of the hash change, leaving the rest identical.
The command throws an error because Linux hashes are case-insensitive
The hash remains identical across both Kali and Termux because the words are technically the same.

title: Terminal hands-on
question: The presenter creates a new file called audit.sh and is immediately denied permission to run it, even though they just created it. Why?
options: Termux's Android sandbox completely prevents custom scripts from running.
The user is logged in as kali instead of root.
In Linux, simply owning a file does not automatically grant you the x (execute) permission to run it as a program.
The ls -la command needs to be run first to unhide the file before execution.

title: Web Security & Input Validation
question: Scenario: A user logs into a web portal. Instead of typing a normal username, they type a special sequence of characters into the input field, which tricks the database into bypassing the password check entirely. What is this common web vulnerability called?
options: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
SQL Injection (SQLi)
Phishing
Data Encryption

title: The CIA Triad
question: During exam week, thousands of college students try to access the online results portal at the exact same time, causing the server to crash completely. Which pillar of the CIA Triad has been violated?
options: Confidentiality
Integrity
Availability
Authentication

title: Terminal hands-on
question: When the presenter runs the command cd /etc on a phone using Termux, what exactly is the user accessing?
options: The actual root control room of the Android operating system.
A private, sandboxed configuration folder located entirely inside Termux's app storage.
A simulated directory that doesn't physically exist on the phone's storage.
A globally shared directory that requires the sudo group to read.

title: Password Security & Termux/Terminal Usage
question: Why are passwords like 123456, password, or those containing your birth year considered dangerously weak by security professionals?
options: They are too long to type quickly on a mobile terminal.
They use special symbols that Termux cannot process.
They can be instantly cracked using automated dictionary and brute-force attacks.
They require a multi-factor authentication token.

title: Phishing
question: Which of the following is one of the most reliable "red flags" that an email might be a phishing attempt?
options: The email addresses you by your full, correct name.
The email arrives on a weekend or holiday.
The sender's email address contains a slight typo or uses an unofficial domain (e.g., support@microsoft-security-alert.com instead of   support@microsoft.com).
The email includes a standard signature block with a company logo.

title: Phishing
question: How does "Spear Phishing" differ from a standard, everyday phishing campaign?
options: Spear phishing uses malicious attachments, whereas standard phishing only uses malicious links.
Spear phishing is highly targeted, using personalized information (like your job title, recent projects, or colleagues' names) to trick a specific individual.
Spear phishing relies on sending identical emails to millions of random addresses hoping a small percentage will click.
Spear phishing only occurs over voice phone calls (Vishing).

title: Phishing
question: You receive an urgent email claiming your bank account will be permanently suspended in 24 hours unless you click a link to verify your password. What is the safest course of action?
options: Click the link, but carefully check if the resulting website's design looks authentic before typing your password.
Reply directly to the email and ask the sender for proof that they are really from the bank
Forward the email to your coworkers to ask for their opinion on whether it looks real.
Do not click the link. Open your web browser, manually type in your bank's official website URL, log in, and check for any secure messages or   alerts.

title: Cyber security basics
question: "What does a pentester do?"
options: They steal data from companies
They find weaknesses in systems with authorization
They protect servers from attacks
They work in banks only

title: Cyber security basics
question: "A cybersecurity expert breaks into a company's system to show them their security gaps. The company hired them to do this. Is this white hat or black hat?"
options: White hat — they had permission
Black hat — breaking in is always illegal
Grey hat — it's risky either way
Neither, it's just consulting

question: "You get an email from 'IT Support' asking you to click a link and verify your password urgently. The email has your company's logo. What threat is this?"
